Need for the Proposed Project
Since the birth of the jet aircraft in 1958, travel times by air have decreased from terminal to terminal. As the efficiency of air travel increases, the effort spent in ground travel becomes a matter of increasing concern to the air traveler.
The Federal Department of Transportation predicts that the number of airline passengers on domestic flights will increase from 150 million in 1970 to 660 million in 1990 nationwide.
Steady growth in air travel demand is now making it mandatory that City, County, State and Federal authorities plan in terms of balanced transportation systems with an increased emphasis on adequate ground access to airports.
The adopted land use and surface transportation plans have considered General Mitchell Field as an important land use concentration and terminal facility and have recommended construction of the Airport Spur Freeway to provide an improved surface transportation facility to serve the passenger, employment, cargo and other activity demands.
The regional airport system plan, currently under preparation by SEWRPC, has identified the need for only one air carrier within the region to serve the forecasted air passenger and cargo demands.
The SEWRPC regional airport system development standards require that the main airport entrance road serving primary scheduled air transport airports, such as General Mitchell Field, shall be directly connected to a freeway on the State Trunk Highway System.
